propositions: The review-bot container needs Bedrock credentials but the instance role grants only SSM read plus KMS decrypt, with no Bedrock permission.
The grant is a scoped inline policy in a new iam_s7.tf attached to the existing rebar-gerrit-instance-role, leaving iam.tf unmodified per its single-owner contract.

The correct IAM actions are bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream scoped to Claude foundation models and inference profiles, because the Converse API authorizes against InvokeModel despite bedrock:Converse existing as a distinct simulatable action.
A scoped policy must be validated by a real from-instance call plus a negative control against a non-Claude model, never from an operator identity holding bedrock:* wildcard which masks the failure.
IMDSv2 reachability from inside the review-bot container is measured first (token PUT returns 200, role resolves) to select the IAM-only path versus a hop-limit contingency.
Operator-attested checks confirm the container authenticates as the scoped role with no static AWS key env vars, and opcert SSM fetch and Gerrit startup remain healthy after apply.
